content: Suffering is not always a pathological phenomenon; rather than being a symptom of neurosis, suffering may well be a human achievement.
author: Viktor Frankl
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Hardship is not an unfair interruption to your real life—it is the very forge in which character is tempered. No one develops deep wisdom, empathy, or stamina by cruising down an easy path without resistance.

Viktor Frankl understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Like a tree that develops deeper roots when buffeted by winter gales, your past trials gave you a reservoir of strength you didn't know you possessed. You are more durable than your anxious thoughts give you credit for.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
